summary: Durnesswick final client report DL_2020_0050 (September 28, 2020) for Nimbravelle Medicines Inc: NM-12 oral vehicle follow-up. The cosolvent-rich vehicle precipitated on aqueous dilution and was rejected; a dispersed suspension was recommended, with practical preparation and administration instructions.
header: DL_2020_0050 | Nimbravelle Medicines Inc | Final Report R1

title_block.title: NM-12 Oral Vehicle: Precipitation-on-Dilution Follow-up
title_block.subtitle: Final Report
lines: Prepared by: Dr J. Carver, Formulation Development Lead

blocks.p: Nimbravelle needed a 10 mg/mL oral vehicle for NM-12 for repeat-dose rodent studies. The cosolvent-rich vehicle selected earlier gave a clear solution but precipitated within minutes when diluted into simulated gastric fluid. We recommend a dispersed suspension in 0.5% HPMC / 0.1% Tween 80, which tolerated dilution and remained dosable for 24 hours.
Eight vehicles were screened at the 10 mg/mL target. Solubility, appearance and 24-hour physical stability are below; this is an exploratory screen, not a locked process.

Each candidate was diluted 1:10 into simulated gastric fluid at 37 °C and observed for 30 minutes. Cosolvent-rich and DMSO-containing vehicles precipitated; the HPMC/Tween suspension and the cyclodextrin solution did not change visibly. The cyclodextrin vehicle was not carried forward because of the dose-volume loading it would need at the top dose.

list: Prepare by wetting the powder with the Tween fraction, then adding HPMC solution in portions with stirring
Stir continuously during dosing; use within 24 hours of preparation
Dose volume 10 mL/kg; check homogeneity at top, middle and bottom before the first dose

blocks.p: Particle size was not controlled; if exposure variability is high in the first study, a milled suspension should be evaluated. Chemical stability of NM-12 in the vehicle beyond 24 hours was not tested.
